episodes.168717: An upper level disturbance, a surface boundary and strong diurnal heating led to numerous severe thunderstorms in the afternoon and evening.
episodes.168736: Numerous afternoon thunderstorms developed across east-central Florida. A few storms became severe in Lake and Orange counties where small hail and wind damage to large trees and homes occurred. Additionally, many of these storms moved over and offshore of the Brevard County coast, where several strong to severe wind gusts were observed.
episodes.168737: Numerous afternoon thunderstorms developed across east-central Florida. Many of these storms moved over and offshore of the Brevard County coast, where several strong to severe wind gusts were observed.
episodes.169032: Deep southerly flow brought sufficient instability and shear to the region. An approaching trough provided sufficient forcing for ascent, resulting in a severe thunderstorm June 17th across primarily Glacier County.
episodes.169033: Deep southerly flow brought sufficient instability and shear to the region. An approaching trough provided sufficient forcing for ascent, resulting in a few severe thunderstorms across western portions of North-central Montana. One supercell dominated, beginning near Lincoln, travelling northeastward, finally crossing the Canadian border at the Blaine/Hill County border.
episodes.169074: An upper trough digging across the Northeast United States with ample shortwave energy helped push a cold front into portions of southeast South Carolina during evening hours, igniting thunderstorms that eventually merged into a mesoscale convective system capable of producing widespread wind damage across an environment displaying moderate levels of mixed layer convective available potential energy and large downdraft convective available potential energy.
episodes.169075: An upper trough digging across the Northeast United States with ample shortwave energy helped push a cold front into portions of southeast Georgia during evening hours, igniting thunderstorms that eventually merged into a mesoscale convective system capable of producing widespread wind damage across an environment displaying moderate levels of mixed layer convective available potential energy and large downdraft convective available potential energy.
episodes.169076: An upper trough digging across the Northeast United States with ample shortwave energy helped push a cold front into portions of local coastal waters during evening hours, igniting thunderstorms that eventually merged into a mesoscale convective system capable of producing widespread wind damage across an environment displaying moderate levels of mixed layer convective available potential energy and large downdraft convective available potential energy.
episodes.169196: Thunderstorms briefly became severe as they passed across the Spearfish area. A few wind gusts around 60 mph were recorded.
episodes.169542: Afternoon thunderstorms produce severe hail, wind gusts and minor flooding across central and southwest Florida.
episodes.169717: Southerly flow brought abundant moisture and instability for scattered thunderstorms during the afternoon.
episodes.169859: A mid-level disturbance sparked a few severe thunderstorms across the area, including a tornado.
episodes.169863: A mid-level disturbance sparked numerous severe thunderstorms across the area.
episodes.169864: A mid-level disturbance sparked numerous strong to severe thunderstorms along the coastal waters.
episodes.169966: A line of thunderstorms became severe and produced numerous reports of wind damage as it moved southward through Eastern NC during the evening hours.
episodes.170144: A cold front encroaching the Ohio Valley on the afternoon of June 17th ran into favorable conditions for strong to severe thunderstorms thanks to abnormally warm temperatures and sufficient low level moisture. Multiple instances of downed trees were observed throughout Lawrence County in response to damaging wind gusts. Heavy downpours, coupled with previous rainfall from days prior, led to Duck Creek and the Little Muskingum River rising out of their banks through the evening hours of the 17th and into the next day. This resulted in minor flooding along adjacent local roads.
episodes.170184: A persistent upper level ridge west of the region started to break down and retrograde with steep mid level lapse rates around 8-9 degC/km. A remnant MCS tracked across the periphery of the weakening ridge west of the area with associated cold pools enhancing convergence over elevated low and mid level instability. These convective ingredients produced strong to severe storms across SE GA in the late afternoon and evening hours.
episodes.171114: The air mass across central Alabama was primed for strong to severe thunderstorms, along with a threat of large hail due to steep mid level lapse rates. A short wave trough digging southward along the Atlantic Coast provided the necessary lift for the development of severe storms.
episodes.171198: A potent upper level disturbance initially brought showers and thunderstorms to the region, but transitioned to a more stratiform event that produced many heavy rain reports.
episodes.171279: A complex of showers and thunderstorms moved across central North Carolina during the late afternoon and evening. The line produced numerous damaging wind gusts along with marginally severe hail. One fatality occurred as the line moved through Franklin County, as a tree fell on and killed a person who was outside.
episodes.171357: A very active summer pattern resulted in numerous reports of trees and power lines down across the tri-state area.  Most of the damage occurred on June 14th as a large MCS moved south and southwestward across most of the area.
episodes.171358: A very active summer pattern resulted in numerous reports of trees and power lines down across the tri-state area.  Most of the damage occurred on June 14th as a large MCS moved south and southwestward across most of the area.
episodes.171491: As high pressure departed the region on the 18th, a warm front lifted across the region. A few isolated thunderstorms developed around midday in association with the warm front and produced some marginally severe hail in a few locations, but were otherwise unremarkable.
episodes.171519: Scattered thunderstorms moved northeast across southeast Arizona. One storm produced a severe wind gust in Green Valley and another caused minor tree damage in Tucson.
episodes.171552: Cold air aloft associated with low pressure over South Florida led to unstable conditions and the development of strong thunderstorms over Southwest Florida and the adjacent Gulf waters.
episodes.171553: Cold air aloft associated with low pressure over South Florida led to unstable conditions and the development of strong thunderstorms over interior South Florida and Lake Okeechobee.
episodes.171626: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds and large hail across portions of central and eastern Virginia.
episodes.171632: Scattered thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced gusty winds across portions of the Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.171651: Strong to severe storms pushed across the northern Red River Valley during the early morning hours.
episodes.171713: A widespread high wind event across Utah was followed by strong thunderstorms associated with a system spanning a three-day period. These storms produced numerous instances of severe wind gusts, in addition to a tornado, a report of hail, and flash flooding.
episodes.171765: A cold front was draped across central Mississippi and Alabama on the 18th of June. A few thunderstorms ahead of this front began to race southwest-ward towards the local area along a weak shortwave system. These storms were able to tap into the local environment that had just enough instability to support a few severe thunderstorms with hail.
episodes.171798: A multi-day severe weather event unfolded mid June as multiple disturbances surrounding the outer periphery of a mid level high pushed through an abnormally moist environment and highly unstable environment over the forecast area. These storms produced numerous reports of trees & powerlines down, quarter to golf ball size hail, structural damage, and isolated instances of flash flooding.

The public relayed pictures via email of many large tree limbs blown down on a property near the Ashley River in North Charleston, including some which damaged a fence. Several trees and numerous large tree branches were also blown down on Flynn Road in Wando Woods Subdivision. Several residences sustained minor damage due to flying debris in strong winds. Damage included broken windows as well as missing roof shingles and pieces of siding.

A National Weather Service Storm Survey Team confirmed straight-line thunderstorm wind damage consistent with an estimated maximum wind speed of 70 to 75 mph in the Wando Woods Subdivision. The most concentrated damage was found along Flynn Drive west of Holbird Street where numerous medium to large trees limbs were snapped off. Flying debris broke a few windows and produced minor shingle and exterior damage to north and west facing surfaces of a few homes. A large trampoline was also propelled 150 feet toward the southeast of its original location and destroyed.
